Catalogue frame-quality scores were unavailable for the WISE frames from 2010 (cryogenic), 2010 (three-band), 2010-2011 (post-cryogenic), so those frames were checked by their measured pixel noise instead.
7 of 366 SPHEREx spectrum points are left out (7 where too much of the target is covered by bad pixels).
The Gaia DR3 and CatWISE2020 lists were reused from the view built on 15 Nov 2026, because the catalogue services did not answer.

The spectrum is not classified because a brighter catalogued source (W1 14.4) 7.3 arcsec away falls inside the area the SPHEREx photometry is fitted over; its light there is estimated at 2 times the target's own, or more.
SPHEREx detects the object at only 12 wavelengths (1.7 to 4.2 µm), which is too little of the spectrum to classify it.
3 detections are left out of the motion fit because a catalogued source of similar brightness lies within the area the position is fitted over.
No single image shows the target clearly enough to measure its position, so its motion was measured by fitting all 23 W2 images at once.
